title: About
text:
Blaise has been working on transport, building and air quality modelling for >15 years. He has excellent knowledge of reproducible data analysis with R.
air quality — dispersion modelling (AERMOD/ADMS), CAMS wildfire PM10 evaluation, NO2 trend/changepoint analysis, met-normalised cycling infrastructure study road safety — STATS19 local authority reports, the Wiltshire 50→40mph appraisal, TAG economic assessment active travel — cycling infrastructure (Barcelona OSM evolution, pop-up lanes/NO2 work), walking/cycling policy transport — the broader umbrella when it’s not specifically active modes meteorology — ERA5 preprocessing pipeline, worldmet/NOAA gap-filling, boundary layer work spatial analysis — LiDAR (solar potential, z0/displacement height), OSM analysis, general GIS reproducible reporting — Quarto pipelines, automated report generation, GitHub Pages publishing R — package development (nexurbr, stats19_stats contributions), Shiny apps (the mapgl spatial audit tool, BAC calculator) dispersion modelling data visualisation shiny open data policy

title: Active Analytics
text:
Active Analytics is an independent consultancy specialising in reproducible analysis of transport, air quality, energy, and road safety data. We build evidence that stands up to scrutiny — from dispersion and energy modelling and meteorological data to STATS19 collision analysis and TAG appraisal.
